Study note: A hypervisor manages virtual machines and isolates their execution environments. A Blue Pill-style attack aims to use virtualization techniques to place a malicious hypervisor beneath an operating system, potentially making the compromise difficult for the guest OS to detect.

questions.question: Which term refers to the independent expectancy between two entities for a specific context at a given time?
questions.explanation:
Trust is the expectation that another entity will behave reliably in a particular context and at a particular time. Reputation reflects others' accumulated opinions, while authentication verifies identity and authorization determines permitted actions.

Study note: Trust is an expectation that another entity will behave dependably in a particular context and at a particular time. In IoT, trust can be based on identity, past behavior, credentials, reputation, and the sensitivity of the action being requested.

questions.question: Which of the following is a feature of the GreenCloud simulator?

options.text: It allows monitoring of energy consumption of networks and devices
It is a closed-source paid software

questions.correctOption: It allows monitoring of energy consumption of networks and devices
questions.explanation:
GreenCloud is a simulator designed to study energy consumption in cloud data-center networks and devices. Monitoring energy use helps researchers compare how network and workload decisions affect power efficiency.

Study note: GreenCloud is a simulator used to study energy-aware cloud and data-center networking. Measuring energy consumption allows researchers to compare design choices, though simulated results still depend on the model assumptions and configuration.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between Microsoft Azure's PaaS (Platform as a Service) and IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) offerings?

options.text: PaaS is free, IaaS is paid
PaaS provides a development environment for clients to build apps, while IaaS offers control over OS and infrastructure
IaaS is for mobile only, PaaS is for web only

questions.correctOption: PaaS provides a development environment for clients to build apps, while IaaS offers control over OS and infrastructure
questions.explanation:
PaaS provides a managed development and deployment platform, while IaaS supplies virtualized infrastructure and gives customers more control over the operating system and environment. The key distinction is the level of the computing stack managed by the provider, not whether one service is free or limited to a device type.

Study note: PaaS abstracts more of the operating system and runtime so developers can deploy applications into a managed environment. IaaS exposes virtual machines and related infrastructure, allowing more control but requiring more administration from the customer.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Java-based cloud simulation platform developed at the University of Melbourne?
questions.explanation:
CloudSim is a Java-based framework for modeling and simulating cloud-computing environments, developed at the University of Melbourne. It lets researchers test scheduling, provisioning, and resource-allocation strategies without building a physical data center.

Study note: CloudSim is a Java-based simulation toolkit used to model cloud data centres, virtual machines, resource allocation, and workload scheduling. It supports repeatable experiments without needing to build a full physical cloud testbed.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used to install OpenStack?
questions.explanation:
DevStack is a set of scripts used to deploy an OpenStack development or test environment. It is mainly intended for learning, development, and experimentation rather than as a production deployment method.

Study note: DevStack is a set of scripts commonly used to install an OpenStack development or test environment. It is convenient for learning and experimentation, but it is not generally recommended as a production deployment method.

questions.question: OpenStack is an open-source software.
questions.explanation:
OpenStack is open-source cloud infrastructure software. Its components can be used to manage compute, networking, storage, identity, and other resources in a private or public cloud environment.

Study note: OpenStack is an open-source cloud platform with services for compute, networking, storage, identity, and other infrastructure functions. Its open-source nature allows organizations to inspect, adapt, and deploy the software, subject to the project’s licenses.

questions.question: If an OpenStack instance must connect to an external public network (for example, the Internet), which component is required between the instance and the public network?
questions.explanation:
A router connects the OpenStack instance's network to an external public network. It provides the routing path between the tenant network and an external network such as the Internet, subject to the configured security and addressing rules.

Study note: A router provides the network path between an OpenStack instance’s private network and an external network. Depending on the deployment, additional configuration such as floating IPs, security groups, and external-network setup may also be needed.

questions.question: Select the statement(s) that denote the limitations of WSNs. Statement I: Procurement Statement II: Deployment Statement III: Maintenance
questions.explanation:
Procurement, deployment, and maintenance are all practical limitations or cost challenges for wireless sensor networks. Devices must be purchased and installed, and distributed nodes later require power management, fault handling, and upkeep.

Study note: WSN procurement involves acquiring appropriate sensors and hardware, deployment involves installing and configuring them, and maintenance involves keeping them operational over time. All three can be difficult because devices may be numerous, distributed, energy-constrained, or placed in hard-to-reach environments.

questions.question: Which of the following are the actors in sensor-cloud?
questions.explanation:
Sensor-cloud systems involve end-users, sensor owners, and the Sensor-Cloud Service Provider (SCSP). Owners supply sensor resources, the provider manages the service layer, and end-users consume the resulting data or applications.

Study note: A sensor-cloud ecosystem can involve sensor owners/providers, cloud or sensor-cloud service providers, and end users or application developers. These actors cooperate to expose sensing capabilities as services rather than requiring every application to manage the physical sensors directly.

questions.question: In sensor-cloud architecture, the managerial role is played by:
questions.explanation:
The Sensor-Cloud Service Provider performs the managerial role in the architecture. It coordinates the sensor resources and service environment so that users can access sensor data through a managed cloud interface.

Study note: The Sensor-Cloud Service Provider manages the service layer that connects physical sensing resources with virtualized sensor services and users. The provider’s role can include resource management, access, service delivery, and coordination between sensors and applications.

questions.question: What is the function of Internal Cache in the caching-based sensor-cloud architecture?

options.text: Decides whether data should be served directly or re-cached from external cache

questions.explanation:
The internal cache can respond to end-user requests and decide whether a result can be served locally or should be fetched/re-cached from an external cache. Both functions reduce unnecessary sensor access and can improve response time and energy efficiency.

Study note: An internal cache can retain recently used sensor data or metadata, reducing repeated access to slower or remote resources. Caching may improve response time and reduce network traffic, while cache freshness and invalidation must be handled to avoid stale results.

questions.question: Unnecessary sensing causes energy consumption.
questions.explanation:
Unnecessary sensing consumes energy without providing proportionate useful information. Scheduling sensing activity and avoiding redundant measurements can extend battery life in sensor-cloud and wireless sensor systems.

Study note: A sensor that measures when no useful observation is needed still consumes energy, especially if sensing and radio communication remain active. Scheduling, event-triggered sensing, and duty cycling can reduce this waste while maintaining required coverage.

questions.question: Dynamic caching mechanism improves the flexibility and efficiency of sensor-cloud.
questions.explanation:
Dynamic caching adapts what is cached to changing requests and data patterns. This can improve flexibility and efficiency by serving frequently requested information quickly and reducing repeated access to remote sensors or services.

Study note: Dynamic caching adjusts what is retained based on demand or changing conditions, rather than using a fixed cache content forever. This can improve hit rate and response time, provided the system manages stale data and cache replacement correctly.

questions.question: Who coined the term Fog computing?
questions.explanation:
Cisco is credited with coining or popularizing the term fog computing. Fog computing brings compute and storage closer to IoT devices, reducing the need to send every operation to a distant cloud.

Study note: Cisco popularized the term “fog computing” for computing, storage, and networking placed closer to the devices that generate data. Fog computing complements cloud computing by supporting low-latency or bandwidth-sensitive tasks near the edge.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks. Fog computing is an intermediate layer between ______ and ______.
questions.explanation:
Fog computing sits between end devices and the cloud. It provides an intermediate layer for local processing, filtering, and time-sensitive decisions before selected data is forwarded to centralized cloud services.

Study note: Devices at the edge generate data, fog nodes process or filter some of it nearby, and cloud systems can handle large-scale storage and analytics. This intermediate layer can reduce latency and the amount of raw data sent across the Internet.

questions.question: Which of the following is/are the types of data with respect to sensitivity?
questions.explanation:
Data can be categorized by how sensitive it is to delay: time-sensitive, less time-sensitive, or not time-sensitive. This classification helps decide whether processing should occur near the device or can tolerate a trip to the cloud.

Study note: Sensitivity categories distinguish how much protection data requires—for example, public, internal, confidential, or highly sensitive information, depending on the framework. Classifying data helps determine access control, storage, retention, and transmission safeguards.

questions.question: Fill in the blank. The concept of ______ enables physical hardware to be shared among multiple entities.
questions.explanation:
Hardware virtualization allows a physical computing resource to be abstracted and shared among multiple virtual machines or tenants. Each virtual environment can behave like a separate machine even though the underlying hardware is shared.

Study note: Hardware virtualization allows one physical server or device to host multiple isolated virtual machines or environments. The entities share physical resources while each can run its own software stack, subject to the limits and security of the virtualization layer.

questions.question: Which of the following is/are advantages of fog computing?
questions.explanation:
Fog nodes can be deployed in different locations and can support mobile or changing environments. Processing near the source can reduce latency and bandwidth use compared with sending every request to a central cloud.

Study note: Fog computing can reduce latency by processing information near its source and can reduce backbone traffic by sending only relevant summaries or events to the cloud. These benefits are especially useful for time-critical IoT applications, although edge nodes have less capacity than large cloud data centres.

questions.question: To what are the fog nodes connected?
questions.explanation:
Fog nodes sit between IoT devices and cloud services, communicating with both sides. They can collect data locally, perform near-device processing, and forward selected results to the cloud for broader storage or analysis.

Study note: Fog nodes may communicate with end devices below them and cloud services above them. They therefore act as an intermediate layer rather than replacing either the edge devices or the cloud.

questions.question: Smart city is an ______ system.
questions.explanation:
A smart city is an urban system that uses information and communication technologies to improve services such as transport, energy, water, public safety, and waste management. The “smart” aspect comes from sensing, connectivity, data analysis, and coordinated control.

Study note: A smart city applies information and communication technologies to urban services such as transport, energy, waste, safety, and water. The objective is to improve efficiency and quality of life, not merely to add connectivity to individual devices.

questions.question: Which of the following is an area of focus in smart parking lots?

options.text: Detection of slots in parking lots

questions.explanation:
Smart parking can combine slot detection, automatic routing to available spaces, and automated charging for electric vehicles. Together these functions can make parking more efficient and reduce unnecessary circulation.

Study note: Smart parking systems may detect vacant spaces, communicate availability, guide drivers, and support monitoring or payment. Together these functions can reduce the time spent searching for parking and improve use of limited urban space.

questions.question: Select the statement(s) that are true for smart health.
questions.explanation:
The supplied answer key identifies Statements I, II, and III as true for smart health. The combined option is appropriate when all listed statements describe valid smart-health capabilities or characteristics in the source material.

Study note: Smart-health systems use connected sensors and information systems for remote monitoring, alerts, and improved access to patient information. The benefits depend on reliable measurements, privacy safeguards, clinical interpretation, and suitable response procedures.

questions.question: What refers to combining information from multiple sensor sources?
questions.explanation:
Multi-sensor data fusion combines information from several sensor sources to produce a more complete or reliable picture. Fusion can reduce uncertainty and compensate for the limitations of any single sensor.

Study note: Multi-sensor data fusion combines observations from different sensors to produce a more complete or reliable estimate than one sensor alone. For example, location, motion, and temperature measurements may be combined to infer context more accurately.

questions.question: The ensemble of all the decisions happens at the ______ level (in data fusion).
questions.explanation:
Decision-level fusion combines the decisions or classifications produced by individual sensors or processing units. It differs from pixel-level or feature-level fusion, which combines lower-level data or extracted features before a final decision.

Study note: Decision-level fusion combines the decisions or conclusions produced by separate sensors or classifiers, rather than combining only raw measurements. This is useful when each source has already performed its own processing and produces a result such as “occupied” or “unoccupied.”

questions.question: The smart parking system reduces traffic ______.
questions.explanation:
Smart parking systems can reduce traffic congestion by helping drivers locate available spaces and reducing the time spent circling. This can also reduce fuel use and emissions associated with searching for parking.

Study note: When a driver can find an available space more quickly, fewer vehicles circulate around a block searching for parking. That reduces congestion and can also reduce fuel use and local emissions.

questions.question: DLNA (used in HAN standards) expands to:
questions.explanation:
DLNA stands for Digital Living Network Alliance. It is associated with standards and guidelines that allow compatible consumer devices to share digital media over a home network.

Study note: DLNA developed guidelines intended to let compatible consumer devices share digital media over a home network. The name expansion is Digital Living Network Alliance; current device interoperability can also depend on newer standards and vendor support.

questions.question: Smart home infrastructure cannot include wireless devices.
questions.explanation:
Smart-home infrastructure can include wireless devices such as Wi-Fi, Zigbee, Bluetooth, or other radio-connected sensors and actuators. Wireless connectivity is often central to installing devices without running new communication cables.

Study note: Smart homes can combine wired and wireless devices, including Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Zigbee, or other technologies. Wireless links are particularly useful where installing new cables would be costly or disruptive.

questions.question: Which of the following is/are layers of Zigbee?
questions.explanation:
Zigbee's protocol stack includes physical and MAC layers along with network-layer functions and application-level services. These layers cover radio transmission, local channel access, network formation/routing, and application communication.

Study note: The Zigbee stack is often described in terms of physical, MAC, network, and application layers, with application support including higher-level profiles and objects. The layers divide responsibilities so radio transmission, access control, routing, and device behavior can be designed separately.

questions.question: Which of the following is a property of V2X?
questions.explanation:
V2X systems use a distributed architecture in which vehicles and other participants exchange information with one another or with infrastructure. This supports cooperative awareness and safety applications without relying on a single source for all information.

Study note: A distributed V2X architecture allows vehicles and other participants to exchange information without relying on one central controller for every local interaction. This can support scalability and resilience, although security, latency, and message authenticity remain essential.

questions.question: CCN is derived from ICN architecture.
questions.explanation:
Content-Centric Networking (CCN) is derived from Information-Centric Networking (ICN) ideas. Rather than identifying communication only by host addresses, it emphasizes requesting and delivering named content through the network.

Study note: Content-Centric Networking is derived from Information-Centric Networking ideas: communication focuses on named content rather than only host addresses. This can support in-network caching and content retrieval from nearby sources when the architecture is designed for it.

questions.question: Fill in the blank. In Vehicle-to-human / human-to-vehicle interaction, the human communicating with the vehicle ______.

options.text: is present in the same vehicle
is present outside the vehicle on the roadside

questions.correctOption: is present outside the vehicle on the roadside
questions.explanation:
In vehicle-to-human or human-to-vehicle roadside interaction, the human is outside the vehicle on the roadside. This distinction separates roadside pedestrian communication from communication with a driver or passenger inside the same vehicle.

Study note: Vehicle-to-human or human-to-vehicle roadside interaction involves a person outside the vehicle, such as a pedestrian or roadside worker, communicating with the vehicle. This is different from an occupant interacting with an in-car interface.

questions.question: Fill in the blank. ICV communication is based on ______.
questions.explanation:
ICV communication in this question uses Dedicated Short Range Communication (DSRC). DSRC is designed for low-latency, short-range vehicle communications supporting safety and traffic applications.

Study note: Dedicated Short-Range Communications (DSRC) was designed for short-range vehicular communication, supporting safety messages and other V2X exchanges. Deployments and standards vary by region, and newer systems may also use cellular V2X.

questions.question: Which of the following is/are domains of VANET?
questions.explanation:
VANETs include an in-vehicle domain and an ad-hoc network domain. The former covers networks inside a vehicle, while the latter supports wireless communication among vehicles and nearby infrastructure.

Study note: VANET domains are commonly divided into vehicle-to-vehicle/ad-hoc communication and infrastructure-based communication involving roadside units. These approaches can complement each other to support safety, traffic information, and service delivery.

questions.question: The vehicles cannot be mobile in the Ad-hoc domain of VANET.
questions.explanation:
Vehicles are mobile in the ad-hoc domain of a VANET; their movement is a defining reason that routes and network topology change over time. The statement claiming they cannot be mobile is therefore false.

Study note: The ad-hoc domain of a VANET is built around moving vehicles that communicate directly or relay messages to one another. Mobility is central to the model and is also what makes topology and routing change rapidly.

questions.question: Which of the following is also used as a name for Smart Grids?
questions.explanation:
The smart grid is also called the energy internet because it connects electricity infrastructure with sensing, communication, and control. This enables more informed coordination between producers, grid operators, distributed resources, and consumers.

Study note: The “energy internet” label emphasizes a connected electricity system with sensing, communications, distributed generation, storage, and flexible demand. It is another way of describing the smart grid’s information-enabled coordination of energy resources.

questions.question: Smart Grid enables which type of energy flow?
questions.explanation:
A smart grid can support bidirectional energy flow because distributed generation and storage—such as rooftop solar and batteries—may both consume and supply electricity. This differs from a purely one-way model from central generation to consumers.

Study note: Traditional grids mainly deliver electricity from large generators toward consumers, whereas smart grids can support two-way flows as consumers also generate or store electricity. Examples include rooftop solar and batteries that can export energy when conditions permit.

questions.question: Fill in the blank. In ________, a home can draw power from distributed resources.
questions.explanation:
Islanding is the condition in which a local power system becomes electrically separated from the main grid but continues to supply a local area using distributed resources. The system must be designed and protected carefully to ensure safe operation.

Study note: Islanding occurs when a local electrical section is disconnected from the main utility grid but continues to be supplied by local distributed resources. It requires appropriate controls and protection so the island remains stable and does not endanger workers or equipment.

questions.question: Fill in the blank. ________ samples voltage and current with a fixed sample rate at the installed location.
questions.explanation:
Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) sample voltage and current waveforms at synchronized sampling rates and estimate their phasors. These measurements help operators observe grid conditions and detect disturbances across the power system.

Study note: PMUs use synchronized timing, commonly from GPS or another precise time source, to produce time-aligned phasor measurements across the grid. This helps compare distant locations and detect oscillations, faults, or instability more quickly than unsynchronized measurements alone.

questions.question: Fill in the blank. ________ is carried out by compromising the availability of a grid component.
questions.explanation:
A denial-of-service attack targets availability by making a grid component or service unavailable, for example by overwhelming it with requests or disrupting its operation. It differs from data-injection attacks, which aim to corrupt measurements or control inputs.

Study note: A denial-of-service attack targets availability, preventing authorized users or components from receiving service. In a grid, disruption may affect monitoring or control, so network resilience and incident response are important alongside confidentiality and integrity.

questions.question: Which of the following are types of Dynamic System Attacks?
questions.explanation:
Replay attacks reuse previously captured messages, dynamic data-injection attacks manipulate measurements, and covert attacks attempt to evade detection while affecting system behavior. All are examples of attacks against dynamic systems.

Study note: Replay attacks resend captured messages, data-injection attacks alter measurements or commands, and covert attacks attempt to manipulate system behavior while avoiding detection. These attacks threaten different aspects of system integrity and observability.

questions.question: State True or False. Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) follows the "rip & replace" approach.
questions.explanation:
IIoT does not generally require a “rip and replace” approach in which all existing infrastructure is discarded. Integrating new sensors, connectivity, and analytics with legacy industrial equipment is a central practical challenge.

Study note: Replacing every legacy industrial device at once is expensive and often impractical. IIoT projects usually aim to integrate new connectivity and analytics with existing equipment where feasible, while addressing compatibility, safety, and cybersecurity.

questions.question: State True or False. Mechanized production is a part of the 4th Industrial Revolution.
questions.explanation:
Mechanized production is associated with the First Industrial Revolution, driven by water and steam power. The Fourth Industrial Revolution is associated with connected cyber-physical systems, automation, data, and the Industrial Internet of Things.

Study note: Mechanized production is the hallmark of the First Industrial Revolution, associated with steam and water power. The Fourth Revolution emphasizes connected cyber-physical systems, industrial IoT, data analytics, and increasingly autonomous processes.

questions.question: Match the Industrial Revolution with the corresponding milestone: 1) 1st 2) 2nd 3) 3rd 4) 4th

options.text: 1-Mechanized production, 2-Mass production, 3-Internet evolution & automation, 4-Industrial Internet of Things

questions.correctOption: 1-Mechanized production, 2-Mass production, 3-Internet evolution & automation, 4-Industrial Internet of Things
questions.explanation:
The correct historical sequence is: first, mechanized production; second, mass production; third, electronics/computing-driven automation and the evolution of the Internet; and fourth, the Industrial Internet of Things. Each stage builds on earlier advances while introducing a different production and connectivity model.

Study note: The sequence moves from mechanization, to electrically powered mass production, to electronics and computer-based automation, and then to connected cyber-physical production. The stages overlap in real factories, but the sequence is a useful exam framework for their defining technologies.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to improve interoperability across different systems?
questions.explanation:
Standardization gives different systems shared protocols, formats, and interfaces, making it easier for them to exchange information. Optimization or monitoring alone does not ensure that independently designed systems interpret one another's messages consistently.

Study note: Shared standards define common interfaces, message formats, and communication rules so independently built systems can exchange data predictably. Standards do not automatically guarantee semantic agreement, but they reduce many compatibility barriers.

questions.question: Fill in the blank. ________ is a primary challenge in IIoT.

options.text: Integrating existing infrastructure into new IIoT infrastructure

questions.correctOption: Integrating existing infrastructure into new IIoT infrastructure
questions.explanation:
Integrating existing infrastructure into new IIoT systems is a major challenge because legacy machines may use older protocols, limited interfaces, or incompatible data formats. Integration must preserve reliability and safety while adding connectivity and analytics.

Study note: Legacy equipment may use proprietary protocols, outdated interfaces, or formats that modern platforms do not understand. Successful integration often requires gateways, adapters, staged migration, and security controls that avoid interrupting production.

questions.question: State True or False. Lack of vision and leadership is not a hindrance in the path of success of IIoT.
questions.explanation:
Lack of vision and leadership can hinder IIoT adoption by leaving goals, investment, responsibilities, and change management unclear. The statement says it is not a hindrance, so it is false.

Study note: Leadership helps set the IIoT goals, fund the necessary infrastructure, assign ownership, and manage organizational change. Without clear direction, projects may remain disconnected pilots or fail to address workforce, process, and cybersecurity needs.

questions.question: State True or False. Big data is characterized by 7 Vs.
questions.explanation:
The source treats big data as characterized by seven Vs, extending the familiar volume, velocity, and variety dimensions with additional properties such as veracity and value. The exact list can vary by framework, but the course's stated convention is seven Vs.

Study note: Commonly listed big-data Vs include volume, velocity, variety, veracity, value, variability, and visualization, although the exact set differs by framework. The point is that large-scale data challenges involve more than just the amount of data.

questions.question: What is the correct flow of data processing?
questions.explanation:
The answer key gives the flow as Generation → Acquisition → Storage → Analysis. Data is first produced by the process or device, then collected, stored for access, and analyzed to extract information or support decisions.

Study note: Generation creates the data, acquisition collects it from sensors or systems, storage retains it, and analysis extracts patterns or decisions. Some real pipelines add cleaning, transformation, and visualization between these stages, but the source’s sequence captures the main flow.

questions.question: Hadoop is primarily used for:
questions.explanation:
Hadoop is a framework for storing and processing large datasets across clusters of computers. Its distributed storage and processing tools let workloads be split across multiple machines, so both listed descriptions apply.

Study note: Hadoop supports distributed storage and processing so large datasets can be split across a cluster instead of relying on one machine. Its ecosystem includes components for storage and batch processing, but it is not itself a single database or one analysis algorithm.

questions.question: The two broad types of data analysis are ______ and ______.
questions.explanation:
Qualitative analysis examines non-numeric characteristics, meanings, and categories, while quantitative analysis works with numerical measurements and statistical methods. Together they represent two broad approaches to analyzing data.

Study note: Qualitative methods examine meanings, descriptions, categories, and observed experiences; quantitative methods analyze numerical measurements using calculations and statistical models. The choice depends on the research question and the kind of evidence collected.

questions.question: Which of the following is/are the basic principle(s) of qualitative analysis?
questions.explanation:
Qualitative analysis involves noticing observations, thinking critically about what they mean, and collecting or organizing relevant evidence. These steps support interpreting patterns and developing explanations from non-numeric data.

Study note: Qualitative analysis usually involves observing or collecting evidence, organizing it, interpreting patterns, and critically checking possible explanations. It is systematic rather than simply subjective: researchers should document how conclusions were reached.

questions.question: To perform an ANOVA, we must have a _____ response variable and at least one _____ factor.
questions.explanation:
ANOVA typically compares group means using a continuous response variable and one or more categorical explanatory factors. The categories define the groups, while the continuous outcome is the measurement being compared.

Study note: ANOVA compares means across groups using a continuous response, such as measured temperature or response time, and a categorical factor, such as treatment group or device type. Its assumptions and design determine whether a standard ANOVA is appropriate.

questions.question: Which of the following is/are application(s) of IoT in agriculture?
questions.explanation:
IoT can support automated irrigation, automated weeding, and water-level monitoring in agriculture. Sensors provide current field conditions and connected controllers can use those measurements to trigger or optimize farm operations.

Study note: IoT agriculture uses sensors and connected control to monitor conditions and automate tasks such as irrigation or weeding. These systems can reduce wasted inputs, but their effectiveness depends on sensor placement, calibration, connectivity, and the quality of control rules.

questions.question: The two most directly relevant sensors used in agriculture (as discussed) are ______.

options.text: Soil moisture and water level sensor
ECG sensor and water level sensor

questions.correctOption: Soil moisture and water level sensor
questions.explanation:
Soil-moisture sensors measure water available in the soil, while water-level sensors monitor the level in a tank, reservoir, or irrigation source. Together they help manage irrigation demand and water availability.

Study note: Soil-moisture data indicates whether plants need water, while a water-level sensor checks whether a tank, canal, or reservoir has enough supply. Using both helps distinguish “the field is dry” from “there is insufficient water available to irrigate.”

questions.question: The deployed IoT gateway of AgriSens communicates with the remote server using:
questions.explanation:
The AgriSens gateway is described as communicating with the remote server over GPRS, a cellular packet-data service. Cellular connectivity lets a field deployment send measurements from locations without local Wi-Fi coverage.

Study note: GPRS is a packet-data service over cellular networks, allowing a remote gateway to transmit readings where wired Internet or local Wi-Fi may be unavailable. Its bandwidth and latency are modest by modern standards, but it has been used for remote telemetry.

questions.question: Select the correct order of component layers in IoT healthcare.

options.text: Sensing layer, cloud platform layer, aggregated layer, processing layer
Sensing layer, aggregated layer, processing layer, cloud platform layer
Aggregated layer, sensing layer, processing layer, cloud platform layer
Sensing layer, processing layer, aggregated layer, cloud platform layer

questions.correctOption: Sensing layer, aggregated layer, processing layer, cloud platform layer
questions.explanation:
The order is sensing layer → aggregated layer → processing layer → cloud platform layer. Data is first collected, then aggregated, processed, and made available to cloud services for storage, analysis, or remote access.

Study note: The sensing layer acquires patient or environment measurements; the aggregation layer gathers data from sources; the processing layer interprets it; and the cloud platform supports storage and broader services. This pipeline separates data collection from analysis and remote access.

questions.question: In AmbuSens, which communication protocol is used?
questions.explanation:
IEEE 802.15.1 is the IEEE standard associated historically with Bluetooth personal-area networking. The other listed standards refer to different technologies or functions, so IEEE 802.15.1 is the expected answer in this course context.

Study note: IEEE 802.15.1 is historically associated with Bluetooth wireless personal-area networks. In modern standards references, Bluetooth specifications have evolved beyond the older IEEE standard, but 802.15.1 is the expected answer for this course item.

questions.question: Wireless IoT-driven remote healthcare provisioning brings healthcare to patients rather than bringing patients to healthcare.
questions.explanation:
Remote IoT healthcare can bring monitoring and selected care services to patients through connected sensors and communication links. This can reduce the need for patients to travel for every observation, although it does not replace all in-person care.

Study note: Remote monitoring can transmit measurements and alerts to clinicians or caregivers without requiring a patient to travel for every routine observation. It complements rather than replaces in-person examination, emergency care, and professional judgment when those are needed.

questions.question: Which handheld device sensor pair is used for activity monitoring (as discussed)?
questions.explanation:
An accelerometer measures movement and changes in acceleration, while GPS can estimate location and movement outdoors. Together they can help characterize a person's activity and context in a handheld monitoring system.

Study note: An accelerometer records changes in acceleration and movement, while GPS estimates geographic position and movement outdoors. Combining them can help distinguish activity patterns and place them in context, though GPS may be unreliable indoors or in dense urban areas.

questions.question: Which of the following is a property of in-place data analysis for activity monitoring?
questions.explanation:
In-place analysis processes activity data on the device itself, so it can be power-intensive but may also reduce network dependence and latency. The “All of these” option captures the properties listed in the question.

Study note: In-place analysis processes data on the handheld device rather than sending every raw sample elsewhere. This can reduce network use and response latency, but it may consume battery and processor resources; the trade-off depends on the model and workload.

questions.question: Deep learning-based analysis cannot be performed on videos.
questions.explanation:
Deep-learning models can analyze video for tasks such as object recognition, activity recognition, and event detection. Video analysis can be computationally demanding, but it is certainly possible with suitable models and hardware.

questions.question: Which of the following are inbuilt sensors present in high-end smartphones (as discussed)?
questions.explanation:
High-end smartphones commonly include accelerometers, compasses or magnetometers, and gyroscopes. These sensors support motion detection, orientation estimation, and navigation; ECG, EEG, and NPK sensors are not standard built-in smartphone sensors.

Study note: Accelerometers measure motion, gyroscopes measure angular velocity, and a compass typically uses a magnetometer to estimate heading. Together they support orientation and navigation; ECG/EEG and agricultural NPK sensing are not ordinary built-in sensors in high-end smartphones.

questions.question: Processing the handheld activity device data using artificial intelligence can be used for ______.
questions.explanation:
AI analysis of accelerometer or other activity-device data can identify patterns associated with falls. Such systems can raise alerts, though real-world use requires validation to limit missed detections and false alarms.

Study note: Fall-detection systems look for motion patterns such as a rapid change in acceleration followed by a period of unusual inactivity. AI can improve classification, but practical systems must be evaluated across different users and movements to reduce false alarms and missed falls.

questions.question: Continuous monitoring of a person’s activity can help observe behavior and identify repetitive patterns.
questions.explanation:
Continuous activity monitoring creates a time series that can reveal routines, repeated actions, and deviations from usual behavior. The interpretation depends on sensor quality and context, but the basic statement is true.

Study note: A continuous record can reveal a person’s usual activity schedule and identify changes, repeated movements, or unusual inactivity. Interpretation should consider context and consent, since the same sensor pattern can have different meanings for different people.
